Long answer: You can simulate memory pressure in user space, but you cannot create real virtual RAM (swap) or expand memory beyond the cgroup limit.

What “virtual RAM” actually means (Linux reality)
On Linux, virtual RAM usually refers to swap:

Swap = disk-backed pages used when RAM is full

Implemented by the kernel
